{{Short description|Family of continuous probability distributions}}
{{More footnotes|date=September 2015}}
{{DISPLAYTITLE:Skewed generalized ''t'' distribution}}
In [[probability]] and [[statistics]], the skewed generalized "t" distribution is a family of continuous [[probability distribution]]s. The distribution was first introduced by Panayiotis Theodossiou<ref name="theodossiou" /> in 1998. The distribution has since been used in different applications.<ref name="hansen1" /><ref name="hansen2" /><ref name="mcdonald1" /><ref name="mcdonald2" /><ref name="mcdonald3" /><ref name="savva" /> There are different parameterizations for the skewed generalized t distribution.<ref name="theodossiou" /><ref name="mcdonald2" />

==Definition==

===Probability density function===

<math>f_\text{SGT}(x; \mu, \sigma, \lambda, p, q) = \frac{p}{2 v \sigma  q^{\frac{1}{p}} B(\frac{1}{p},q) \left[1 + \frac{| x-\mu + m |^p}{q (v \sigma)^p (1 + \lambda \sgn(x-\mu + m))^p}\right]^{\frac{1}{p}+q}}</math>

where <math>B</math> is the [[beta function]], <math>\mu</math> is the location parameter, <math>\sigma > 0</math> is the scale parameter, <math>-1 < \lambda < 1</math> is the skewness parameter, and <math>p > 0</math> and <math>q > 0</math> are the parameters that control the [[kurtosis]]. <math>m</math> and <math>v</math> are not parameters, but functions of the other parameters that are used here to scale or shift the distribution appropriately to match the various parameterizations of this distribution.

In the original parameterization<ref name="theodossiou" /> of the skewed generalized t distribution, 
:<math>m =   \lambda v \sigma \frac{2 q^{\frac{1}{p}} B(\frac{2}{p},q-\frac{1}{p})}{B(\frac{1}{p},q)} </math> 
and 
:<math>v = \frac{q^{-\frac{1}{p}}}{\sqrt{ (1 + 3 \lambda^2)  \frac{ B ( \frac{3}{p}, q - \frac{2}{p} )}{B (\frac{1}{p}, q )}  -4 \lambda^2 \frac{B ( \frac{2}{p}, q - \frac{1}{p} )^2}{ B (\frac{1}{p}, q )^2}}}</math>.
These values for <math>m</math> and <math>v</math> yield a distribution with mean of <math>\mu</math> if <math>pq > 1</math> and a variance of <math>\sigma^2</math> if <math>pq > 2</math>. In order for <math>m</math> to take on this value however, it must be the case that <math>pq > 1</math>. Similarly, for <math>v</math> to equal the above value, <math>pq > 2</math>.

The parameterization that yields the simplest functional form of the probability density function sets <math>m = 0</math> and <math>v = 1</math>. This gives a mean of
:<math>\mu+ \frac{2 v \sigma \lambda q^{\frac{1}{p}} B(\frac{2}{p},q-\frac{1}{p})}{B(\frac{1}{p},q)} </math>
and a variance of
:<math> \sigma^2 q^{\frac{2}{p}} ( (1 + 3 \lambda^2) \frac{ B ( \frac{3}{p}, q - \frac{2}{p} )}{B (\frac{1}{p}, q )} -4 \lambda^2 \frac{B ( \frac{2}{p}, q - \frac{1}{p} )^2}{ B (\frac{1}{p}, q )^2}) </math>

The <math>\lambda</math> parameter controls the skewness of the distribution. To see this, let <math>M</math> denote the mode of the distribution, and 
:<math>
\int_{-\infty}^{M}  f_\text{SGT}(x; \mu, \sigma, \lambda, p, q) \mathrm{d}x = \frac{1-\lambda}{2}
</math>

Since <math>-1 < \lambda < 1</math>, the probability left of the mode, and therefore right of the mode as well, can equal any value in (0,1) depending on the value of <math>\lambda</math>. Thus the skewed generalized t distribution can be highly skewed as well as symmetric. If <math>-1 < \lambda < 0</math>, then the distribution is negatively skewed. If <math>0 < \lambda < 1</math>, then the distribution is positively skewed. If <math>\lambda = 0</math>, then the distribution is symmetric.

Finally, <math>p</math> and <math>q</math> control the kurtosis of the distribution. As <math>p</math> and <math>q</math> get smaller, the kurtosis increases<ref name="theodossiou" /> (i.e. becomes more leptokurtic). Large values of <math>p</math> and <math>q</math> yield a distribution that is more platykurtic.

===Moments===

Let <math>X</math> be a random variable distributed with the skewed generalized t distribution. The <math>h^{th}</math> moment (i.e. <math>E[(X- E(X))^h]</math>), for <math>pq > h</math>, is:
<math>
 \sum_{r=0}^{h} \binom{h}{r} ((1+\lambda)^{r+1}+(-1)^r (1-\lambda)^{r+1} ) ( - \lambda )^{h-r} \frac{ (v \sigma)^h q^{\frac{h}{p}} B(\frac{r+1}{p},q-\frac{r}{p}) B(\frac{2}{p},q-\frac{1}{p} )^{h-r}}{ 2^{r-h+1} B(\frac{1}{p},q)^{h-r+1} }
</math>

The mean, for <math>pq > 1</math>, is:
:<math>
\mu + \frac{2 v \sigma \lambda q^{\frac{1}{p}} B(\frac{2}{p},q-\frac{1}{p})}{B(\frac{1}{p},q)} - m
</math>

The variance (i.e. <math>E[(X- E(X))^2]</math>), for <math>pq > 2</math>, is:
:<math> 
(v \sigma)^2 q^{\frac{2}{p}} ( (1 + 3 \lambda^2) \frac{ B ( \frac{3}{p}, q - \frac{2}{p} )}{B (\frac{1}{p}, q )} -4 \lambda^2 \frac{B ( \frac{2}{p}, q - \frac{1}{p} )^2}{ B (\frac{1}{p}, q )^2})
</math>

The skewness (i.e. <math>E[(X- E(X))^3]</math>), for <math>pq > 3</math>, is:
:<math>
\frac{2 q^{3/p} \lambda  (v \sigma) ^3}{B(\frac{1}{p},q)^3} \Bigg( 8 \lambda ^2 B(\frac{2}{p},q-\frac{1}{p})^3-3 (1+3 \lambda ^2) B(\frac{1}{p},q)
</math>
:<math>
\times B(\frac{2}{p},q-\frac{1}{p}) B(\frac{3}{p},q-\frac{2}{p})+2
(1+\lambda ^2) B(\frac{1}{p},q)^2 B(\frac{4}{p},q-\frac{3}{p}) \Bigg)
</math>

The kurtosis (i.e. <math>E[(X- E(X))^4]</math>), for <math>pq > 4</math>, is:
:<math>
\frac{q^{4/p} (v \sigma) ^4}{B(\frac{1}{p},q)^4} \Bigg( -48 \lambda ^4 B(\frac{2}{p},q-\frac{1}{p})^4+24
\lambda ^2 (1+3 \lambda ^2) B(\frac{1}{p},q) B(\frac{2}{p},q-\frac{1}{p})^2 
</math>
:<math>
\times B(\frac{3}{p},q-\frac{2}{p})-32
\lambda ^2 (1+\lambda ^2) B(\frac{1}{p},q)^2 B(\frac{2}{p},q-\frac{1}{p}) B(\frac{4}{p},q-\frac{3}{p})
</math>
:<math>
+(1+10
\lambda ^2+5 \lambda ^4) B(\frac{1}{p},q)^3 B(\frac{5}{p},q-\frac{4}{p})\Bigg)
</math>

==Special Cases==

Special and limiting cases of the skewed generalized t distribution include the skewed generalized error distribution, the generalized t distribution introduced by McDonald and Newey,<ref name="mcdonald3" /> the skewed t proposed by Hansen,<ref name="hansen" /> the skewed Laplace distribution, the generalized error distribution (also known as the [[generalized normal distribution]]), a skewed normal distribution, the [[student t distribution]], the skewed Cauchy distribution, the [[Laplace distribution]], the [[uniform distribution (continuous)|uniform distribution]], the [[normal distribution]], and the [[Cauchy distribution]]. The graphic below, adapted from Hansen, McDonald, and Newey,<ref name="hansen1" /> shows which parameters should be set to obtain some of the different special values of the skewed generalized t distribution.

[[File:SGTtree.png|thumb|The skewed generalized t distribution tree]]

===Skewed generalized error distribution===
The Skewed Generalized Error Distribution (SGED) has the pdf:
:<math> 
\lim_{q\to\infty} f_\text{SGT}(x; \mu, \sigma, \lambda, p, q) 
</math>
:<math>
= f_\text{SGED}(x; \mu, \sigma, \lambda, p) = \frac{p}{2 v \sigma \Gamma ( \frac{1}{p} )} e^{- \left( \frac{|x - \mu + m|}{ v \sigma [1 + \lambda \sgn(x - \mu + m)]} \right)^p }
</math>
where 
:<math>
m = \lambda v \sigma \frac{ 2^{ \frac{2}{p} } \Gamma ( \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{p} ) }{ \sqrt{\pi}}
</math>
gives a mean of <math>\mu</math>. Also
:<math>
v = \sqrt{\frac{\pi  \Gamma(\frac{1}{p})}{ \pi
 (1+3 \lambda ^2) \Gamma( \frac{3}{p})-16^{\frac{1}{p}} \lambda ^2 \Gamma(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{p})^2 \Gamma(\frac{1}{p})}}
</math>
gives a variance of <math>\sigma^2</math>.

===Generalized ''t''-distribution===
The generalized ''t''-distribution (GT) has the pdf:  
:<math> 
f_\text{SGT}(x; \mu, \sigma, \lambda{=}0, p, q) 
</math>
:<math> 
= f_\text{GT}(x; \mu, \sigma, p, q) = \frac{p}{2 v \sigma  q^{\frac{1}{p}} B(\frac{1}{p},q) \left[1 + \frac{\left| x-\mu \right| ^p}{q (v \sigma) ^p }\right]^{\frac{1}{p}+q}}
</math>
where 
:<math>
v = \frac{1}{q^{\frac{1}{p}}} \sqrt{\frac{ B(\frac{1}{p},q) }{ B(\frac{3}{p},q-\frac{2}{p}) }}
</math>
gives a variance of <math>\sigma^2</math>.

===Skewed ''t''-distribution===
The skewed ''t''-distribution (ST) has the pdf:
:<math> 
f_\text{SGT}(x; \mu, \sigma, \lambda, p{=}2, q) 
</math>
:<math> 
= f_\text{ST}(x; \mu, \sigma, \lambda, q) = \frac{\Gamma ( \frac{1}{2}+q )}{v \sigma (\pi q)^{\frac{1}{2}} \Gamma (q) \left[ 1 + \frac{\left| x-\mu + m \right| ^2}{q (v \sigma) ^2 (1+\lambda \sgn(x-\mu + m))^2}\right]^{\frac{1}{2}+q}}
</math>
where 
:<math>
m = \lambda v \sigma \frac{2 q^{\frac{1}{2}} \Gamma (q-\frac{1}{2})}{\pi^{\frac{1}{2}} \Gamma (q)}
</math>
gives a mean of <math>\mu</math>. Also
:<math>
v = \frac{1}{q^{\frac{1}{2}} \sqrt{ (1 + 3 \lambda^2) \frac{1}{2q-2} -\frac{4 \lambda^2}{\pi} \left( \frac{\Gamma ( q - \frac{1}{2} )}{ \Gamma ( q )} \right)^2 }}
</math>
gives a variance of <math>\sigma^2</math>.

===Skewed Laplace distribution===
The skewed Laplace distribution (SLaplace) has the pdf:
:<math> 
\lim_{q\to\infty} f_\text{SGT}(x; \mu, \sigma, \lambda, p{=}1, q) 
</math>
:<math>
= f_\text{SLaplace}(x; \mu, \sigma, \lambda) = \frac{1}{2 v \sigma} e^{- \frac{ |x - \mu + m|}{ v \sigma (1 + \lambda \sgn(x - \mu + m))} }
</math>
where 
:<math>
m = 2 v \sigma \lambda
</math>
gives a mean of <math>\mu</math>. Also
:<math>
v = [ 2 (1+\lambda ^2) ]^{-\frac{1}{2}}
</math>
gives a variance of <math>\sigma^2</math>.

===Generalized error distribution===
The generalized error distribution (GED, also known as the [[generalized normal distribution]]) has the pdf:
:<math> 
\lim_{q\to\infty} f_\text{SGT}(x; \mu, \sigma, \lambda{=}0, p, q) 
</math>
:<math>
= f_\text{GED}(x; \mu, \sigma, p) = \frac{p}{2 v \sigma \Gamma ( \frac{1}{p} )} e^{- \left( \frac{|x - \mu|}{ v \sigma} \right)^p }
</math>
where 
:<math>
v = \sqrt{ \frac{\Gamma ( \frac{1}{p} )}{ \Gamma ( \frac{3}{p} )}}
</math>
gives a variance of <math>\sigma^2</math>.

===Skewed normal distribution===
The skewed normal distribution (SNormal) has the pdf:
:<math> 
\lim_{q\to\infty} f_\text{SGT}(x; \mu, \sigma, \lambda, p{=}2, q) 
</math>
:<math>
= f_\text{SNormal}(x; \mu, \sigma, \lambda) = \frac{1}{v \sigma \sqrt{\pi}} e^{- \left[ \frac{|x - \mu + m|}{ v \sigma (1 + \lambda \sgn(x - \mu + m))} \right]^2 }
</math>
where 
:<math>
m =  \lambda v \sigma \frac{ 2 }{ \sqrt{\pi}}
</math>
gives a mean of <math>\mu</math>. Also
:<math>
v = \sqrt{\frac{2 \pi }{ \pi -8 \lambda ^2+3 \pi  \lambda ^2} }
</math>
gives a variance of <math>\sigma^2</math>.

The distribution should not be confused with the [[skew normal distribution]] or another [[Generalized normal distribution#Asymmetric version|asymmetric version]]. Indeed, the distribution here is a special case of a bi-Gaussian, whose left and right widths are proportional to <math>1-\lambda</math> and <math>1+\lambda</math>.

===Student's ''t''-distribution===
The [[Student's t-distribution]] (T) has the pdf:
:<math> 
f_\text{SGT}(x; \mu{=}0, \sigma{=}1, \lambda{=}0, p{=}2, q{=}\tfrac{d}{2}) 
</math>
:<math> 
= f_\text{T}(x; d) = \frac{\Gamma ( \frac{d+1}{2} )}{ (\pi d)^{\frac{1}{2}} \Gamma (\frac{d}{2})}  \left(1 + \frac{x^2}{d}\right)^{-\frac{d+1}{2}}
</math>
<math>v = \sqrt{2}</math> was substituted.

===Skewed Cauchy distribution===
The skewed cauchy distribution (SCauchy) has the pdf:
:<math> 
f_\text{SGT}(x; \mu, \sigma, \lambda, p{=}2, q{=}\tfrac{1}{2}) 
</math>
:<math> 
= f_\text{SCauchy}(x; \mu, \sigma, \lambda) = \frac{1}{\sigma \pi \left[1 + \frac{\left| x-\mu \right| ^2}{ \sigma ^2 (1+\lambda \sgn(x-\mu ))^2}\right]}
</math>
<math>v = \sqrt{2}</math> and <math>m = 0</math> was substituted.

The mean, variance, skewness, and kurtosis of the skewed Cauchy distribution are all undefined.

===Laplace distribution===
The [[Laplace distribution]] has the pdf:
:<math> 
\lim_{q\to\infty} f_\text{SGT}(x; \mu, \sigma, \lambda{=}0, p{=}1, q) 
</math>
:<math>
= f_\text{Laplace}(x; \mu, \sigma) = \frac{1}{2 \sigma } e^{ -\frac{|x - \mu|}{ \sigma } }
</math>
<math>v = 1</math> was substituted.

===Uniform distribution===
The [[Uniform distribution (continuous)|uniform distribution]] has the pdf:
:<math> 
\lim_{p\to\infty} f_\text{SGT}(x; \mu, \sigma, \lambda, p, q) 
</math>
:<math>
 = f(x)=\begin{cases}
  \frac{1}{2 v \sigma} & |x - \mu| < v \sigma \\
  0 & \mathrm{otherwise}
  \end{cases} 
</math>
Thus the standard uniform parameterization is obtained if <math>\mu = \frac{a+b}{2}</math>, <math>v = 1</math>, and <math>\sigma = \frac{b-a}{2}</math>.

===Normal distribution===
The [[normal distribution]] has the pdf:
:<math>
\lim_{q\to\infty} f_\text{SGT}(x; \mu, \sigma, \lambda{=}0, p{=}2, q) 
</math>
:<math>
= f_\text{Normal}(x; \mu, \sigma) = \frac{e^{- \left( \frac{|x - \mu|}{ v \sigma } \right)^2 }}{v \sigma \sqrt{\pi}}
</math>
where 
:<math>
v = \sqrt{2}
</math>
gives a variance of <math>\sigma^2</math>.

===Cauchy Distribution===
The [[Cauchy distribution]] has the pdf:
:<math> 
f_\text{SGT}(x; \mu, \sigma, \lambda{=}0, p{=}2, q{=}\tfrac{1}{2}) 
</math>
:<math> 
= f_\text{Cauchy}(x; \mu, \sigma) = \frac{1}{ \sigma \pi \left[1 + \left( \frac{x- \mu}{\sigma} \right)^2\right]}
</math>
<math>v = \sqrt{2}</math> was substituted.
